title: Wakeword detections are handled even when detection is disabled
reasoning: The bridge event subscription remains active regardless of enabled, and the WAKEWORD_DETECTED handler never checks enabled before applying cooldown, sending WAKEWORD_DISABLE, and invoking onWakewordDetectedRef. The disabled branch asks the main process to disable wakeword capture, but any late or queued detection event after disabled can still fire the user callback and trigger the voice flow.
reproduction: Enable wakeword detection, then disable it and deliver a queued WAKEWORD_DETECTED IPC event after the disabled branch runs. The handler still invokes onWakewordDetectedRef if confidence passes threshold and cooldown has elapsed.
recommendation: Ignore detection events when enabled is false, or unsubscribe/subscribe conditionally so disabled mode cannot invoke the wakeword callback. Keep status events if needed, but gate detection side effects on the current enabled state via a latest ref.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for bridge event behavior, late IPC delivery, or disabled-state callback suppression.
suggestedRegressionTest: Render the hook with enabled false, emit WAKEWORD_DETECTED through a mocked IpcBridge, and assert WAKEWORD_DISABLE and onWakewordDetected are not called.
minimumFixScope: useWakewordBridgeEvents detection handler gating, with a focused hook test around disabled and late-event behavior.
